issues.issue: Farmee must "acquire and/or maintain" three named kinds of insurance with no stated policy limits, deductibles or duration. Whether any particular level of coverage satisfies the covenant cannot be determined from the words.

The section is headed "MODIFICATIONS AND AMENDMENTS" but contains no amendment procedure at all; it is an after-acquired-interest clause, and its reach — "any subsequently acquired interest in such lands ... whether obtained directly or indirectly" — is stated without limit. The mismatch between heading and text is itself a construction problem.

The clause fixes the term by reference to two events only, without any outside date, so if neither occurs the Agreement runs indefinitely. Whether "until such time as" creates a perpetual instrument is open.

Section 13(A) says the Agreement "terminates pursuant to Sections 3(A)(2), 3(B)(3), 3(F), and/or 5(B)", but 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) are bare deadlines containing no termination language and 5(B) terminates only as to Unearned Farmout Lands; 13(B) also assumes "all Farmout Lands" can be earned though Section 2(D) permits earning only 80/40-acre circles. The term provision cannot be squared with the sections it cites.

Farmee must comply with all obligations, burdens and requirements "set forth hereunder or otherwise associated with the lands covered hereby", and the trailing catch-all has no stated source or boundary. What obligations are "otherwise associated with the lands" is entirely undefined.

Farmee must "settle surface damages" and restore the premises "as nearly as possible to its original condition", neither of which supplies a measurable standard or a baseline condition. How near is "as nearly as possible" would have to be construed.

Section 15(D) bars any assignment or encumbrance by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent, while the Exhibit "D" assignment form expressly permits Assignee to assign down to a 25% working interest on mere written notice, requiring consent only for assignment of operator rights. The two assignment regimes conflict.

The right is labelled a "Right of First Refusal" but operates as a fixed-terms option — Farmor must offer before granting any farmout and Farmee accepts on preset terms — with no matching of any third-party offer. "One time" right and the fifteen-day election period compound the uncertainty about what triggers the offer duty.

The condition that Farmee "drills and completes the test well on or before August 31, 1996" is impossible to reconcile with Section 3(A)(2), which requires only that drilling commence by that date, and Section 3(A)(3), which allows 45 days after total depth to complete. The trigger for the right cannot be satisfied on the schedule the Agreement itself sets.

The statement that the terms "shall run with said Farmout Lands" asserts a real covenant without identifying the burdened estate or any privity, leaving open whether it binds successors in title as opposed to contracting parties. That is a classic point of construction in oil and gas instruments.

This clause makes the Agreement binding on "successors and assigns", while Section 15(D) provides the Agreement "may not be assigned, sublet, mortgaged, pledged, encumbered" by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent. Whether assigns can exist at all has to be reconciled between the two.

The Agreement takes effect "as of the date first above written", yet the date lines on Exhibits A, C and D — all incorporated as part of the Agreement by Section 1 — are left blank. Which date governs the incorporated documents is unstated.

The schedule contains internal errors that affect what land is included: tract 228594F (5-1120) is listed twice at 3.65 and 391.60 acres, 228630F (5-1154) twice at .35 and 188.84, 228577F twice, and one entry "(5-1152) 10.12" carries no lease number. The described Farmout Lands cannot be determined with certainty from the list.

The tract schedule must be reconciled with the cover-page description of "5,400 acres, more or less" and with the Exhibit "B" plat, which Section 1 also makes part of the Agreement. A discrepancy between the written schedule and the plat would have to be resolved.

Exhibit C imposes every duty on "Operator", a term the Agreement never defines and never equates with Farmee, although Section 3(D) makes compliance with Exhibit C a condition of earning. Who owes these obligations if Farmee is not the operator is unresolved.

The paragraph requires a "qualified wellsite geologist" to "thoroughly and timely" examine samples and that cores be "properly and timely analyzed", none of which is given a measure. It also grants access to "EREX", an abbreviation used nowhere else in the instrument.

The obligation applies to "significant indications of reservoir quality porosity with hydrocarbon shows" and requires that they be "adequately tested in accordance with good oilfield practices", stacking three undefined standards on one another. Neither significance nor adequacy has any benchmark in the instrument.

The requirement of a "Routine daily prepaid report" appears to be a mechanical error for "prepared", and as written it imposes an unintelligible prepayment condition on the reporting duty. The sentence is also left unpunctuated at its end.

The duty attaches to "Non-routine occurrences such as notification of significant shows, intent to core, test or log", an open illustrative list whose outer boundary is undefined. Whether an occurrence outside the examples must be telephoned immediately is left to argument.

The list of required well surveys is a checkbox schedule whose marks are indeterminate — stray characters appear against Density and Neutron and the "Other" line is blank — so which surveys must actually be run cannot be read off the page. The obligation is left incomplete on its face.

"Timely notice of intent to core, test or log" fixes no period, and the only measure offered is the purpose clause that Farmor's representative "may be present to witness same". How much notice is enough is undetermined.

The lead-in requires "one copy" of the listed items, item (a) requires "Two final prints", and a free-standing heading "THREE COPIES:" precedes items (b) to (e); the number of copies actually owed is internally inconsistent. Item (e), "any other data pertinent", is also an unbounded catch-all.

Operator must furnish "full information on the completion progress, including one copy of the data listed below", so the enumerated items are illustrative of an undefined larger duty. What "full information" beyond the list requires is left open.

Exhibit C directs all reports to a different street address and a different addressee (Mike Stamper, 1989 E. Stone Drive) than Section 10(B) prescribes for notices to Farmor (Two Executive Park Place, Attn: Lester Zitkus). Which address governs well data notices requires reading the two together.

The granting clause depends entirely on blanks — the well number and the size of the "____ acre circle" are never filled in — so the form as incorporated conveys nothing identifiable. The description also refers to an "Exhibit A attached hereto" that does not exist in the form.

Section 2(D) fixes the earned area at an 80-acre circle for gas wells and a 40-acre circle for oil wells, but the assignment form that Section 3(D)(1) says shall be used leaves the acreage open. What is actually conveyed must be reconciled with Section 2(D).

The assignment endures "so long as oil and gas or either of them is produced in paying quantities" or the well is shut in, with no temporary-cessation savings period and no definition of paying quantities. When the assignment ends is precisely the kind of habendum question courts construe.

This habendum keeps the assignment alive while the well is shut in, but Section 5(A) requires Farmee to give notice and plug and abandon a well that "ceases production" or is not capable of paying production, and Section 7(A) conditions shut-in status on payment of a shut-in royalty. The three provisions give different answers for a non-producing well.

The Assignor conveys rights "necessary or convenient" for operations under the underlying deeds or leases, and "convenient" has no ascertainable limit. The scope of the easements and rights of way passing under the clause is therefore open.

The reserved royalty rate and the substance produced are both left blank ("equal to ____ ( __% of 8/8) ... from the sale of ____"), so the form cannot itself fix the reservation. The blanks go to the essential term of the reservation.

This clause reserves the royalty "without deductions of any kind, except that Assignor shall bear its proportionate part of any severance tax", while Section 4(A) of the Farmout Agreement reserves the same royalty "without deductions of any kind" with no exception. The severance-tax carve-out contradicts the governing reservation.

The clause reserves title to "the aforementioned lands, and all rights connected thereto" and then grants "other such rights" — a self-cancelling formula in which the reservation appears to swallow the grant. What was actually conveyed depends on construing that sentence.

The provision limits assignments that would reduce Assignee's "rights and interest in and to Well No. ___" below a "twenty-five percent (25%) working interest", although the instrument conveys operating rights rather than a working interest and never defines the latter. How the 25% floor is measured is unclear.

This clause permits assignments on written notice so long as a 25% interest is retained, whereas Section 15(D) of the Farmout Agreement forbids any assignment or encumbrance by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent. The two consent regimes cannot both govern a transfer of the earned rights.

The reservation of "all strata and formations extending below the ____ formation" leaves the controlling formation blank, so the vertical limit of the assignment is undetermined on the face of the instrument. Nothing in the clause supplies a default.

The reservation is expressed stratigraphically while Section 3(E) of the Farmout Agreement measures the depths earned in footage — surface to 100' below total depth, capped at 4,000'. The two measures of the vertical severance do not correspond.

Binding the assignment on "successors and assigns" sits against Section 15(D) of the Farmout Agreement, which bars assignment by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent. Whether assigns can take free of that restriction requires reading the two together.

Making the assignment "subject to the terms and conditions" of the Farmout Agreement is hard to square with Section 3(F), under which termination of the Agreement leaves Operating Rights Earned intact, and with Section 4's statement that the reserved override survives termination. Whether termination of the Farmout Agreement pulls down the assignment is left open.
